concepts.name_en: Slope shadow: free tube-launched gravity glider that lands ahead in the snow
concepts.name_zh: 坡影：从背管射出、靠重力跟拍、停下时落在前方雪里的自由滑翔机
concepts.one_liner: The I-05 glider without the leash. It ejects from a pack tube once the skier is above 8 m/s and follows on slope energy with servo-only power (2.9 W, 52 min). When the skier slows it overflies and belly-lands 3-4 m past them at 3 J. The skier picks it up and slides it back into the tube.
concepts.principle: Same gravity-following physics as I-05. Without a tether there is no tow on flats and no automatic recovery, so every stop costs a pick-up.

architecture.use_flow: spring/air-flow ejection from shoulder tube at >=8 m/s -> follow -> overfly & land ahead -> pick up (1 action)

footage.why: Same view as I-05 but drops out in headwind.

convenience.why: A pick-up at every stop; no footage in the first ~5 s of each run.

safety.why: Free flyer, 14.9 J cap; lands near people.

tech_risk.why: Headwind and flats ground it; UAS rules apply.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: Gravity alone can carry a camera behind a skier for whole runs on blue/red slopes.
concepts.falsification_test: Sim over the slope mix with real wind: falsified if follow share <70 % in 0-5 m/s wind.
concepts.novelty: web searches 2026-10-19: 'autonomous glider drone follow skier camera unpowered', '"glider" camera follows snowboarder OR skier "no motor"' -> only powered follow drones (HoverAir, Skydio, Staaker, Airdog, Cape) and a powered-UAV follow patent; no unpowered/gravity follower found

user_sequence.action: ski 4 m, pick up, slide into tube

concepts.verdict: TOP-4 (as the simple, tether-free sibling of I-05). Proves the gravity principle cheaply. Biggest risk: headwind (32 % follow at 5 m/s) and a pick-up at every stop.

concepts.name_en: Carrier perch: free glider lands on the moving skier's back
concepts.name_zh: 航母式停靠：滑翔机在行进中落到滑雪者背上
concepts.one_liner: At matched speed the relative velocity between glider and skier is ~0, so the glider could land on a dorsal perch like a plane on a carrier (DLR has landed a UAV on a car at 75 km/h).
concepts.principle: Relative KE at 1.5 m/s is only 0.14 J. The trouble is that the skier's wake has a 32-52 % velocity deficit 1-2 m behind the skier, below the glider's stall speed.

architecture.use_flow: approach from behind-above -> hook dorsal wire

wake_deficit_1m.ref: axisymmetric wake similarity ASSUMED const 0.7, CdA 0.4

originality.why: Car-top landing exists; human-back landing has only HCI studies.

tech_risk.why: The glider stalls in the skier's wake.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: A glider can land on a moving skier.
concepts.falsification_test: CFD/sim of the wake: killed if airspeed at the perch is below 1.1 x stall.

prior_art.name: DLR fixed-wing landing on moving car
prior_art.relevance: matched-speed landing, 0.5 m accuracy, 4x5 m net

prior_art.name: Understanding drone landing on the human body (MobileHCI 2021)

concepts.novelty: Matched-speed landing exists for cars, not for people.
concepts.verdict: KILLED as a free perch: the skier's wake leaves 4.5-6.3 m/s airspeed at 1-2 m, below stall. The idea survives as I-05's line-guided dock, where the reel supplies the energy and the glider doesn't need to fly the final metre.

concepts.name_en: Glide-and-perch tail-sitter: glides on gravity, hovers only to take off, waits standing in the snow
concepts.name_zh: 滑翔-驻停尾座式：重力滑翔跟拍，只在起飞时悬停，停下时立在雪里等待
concepts.one_liner: A free 175-182 g tail-sitter flying wing glides behind the skier on slope energy. At each stop it lands upright in the snow near the skier and waits at zero power, then takes off vertically when the skier moves. Hover is used ~10 s per segment, giving 44 min filming per 7.4 Wh charge against ~9 min for a pure hover.
concepts.principle: Follow drones fail on endurance because they hover the whole time (27-50 W). On slopes, gliding costs about 3 W of avionics power, because gravity pays for the flight. The only unavoidable powered phase is getting airborne from a standstill. Snow lets the aircraft land tail-down and stand at zero power, which removes loitering.

architecture.carrier: flying wing S 0.06 m2 AR 9 with two 5-inch tractor props (folding) on the leading edge; tail-sitter VTOL
architecture.support: wing lift (glide) / prop thrust (10 s take-off, transition)
architecture.energy: gravity on runs + 7.4 Wh 2S for take-offs
architecture.sensing: UWB/GNSS beacon + vision fallback (as round-1 S2 v3)
architecture.imaging: 16 g 4K EIS camera, belly-mounted (horizon in glide, looks forward in hover after reframe)
architecture.use_flow: palm/snow VTOL -> transition -> gravity follow -> on stop: land tail-down upright beside track -> wait -> auto VTOL when skier moves -> end of run lands on glove

viewpoints.notes: plus static 'stop shot' from where it stands

tipover_wind.ref: upright on snow, tail sunk 6 cm (calc_kills_and_variants.py)

footage.why: Free viewpoint plus stop shots. Behind at 7.8 m.

interference.why: Nothing on the body except a holster.

convenience.why: Self-relaunching; actions only at the start and end of a run (palm).

safety.why: Free flyer near other skiers; a 14.9 J cap means it drops behind above 12.8 m/s. Props are live only during take-off.

simplicity.why: Tail-sitter transitions in gusts near snow are hard; snow landing and stand-up need work.

originality.why: No glide-and-perch follow camera product found; tail-sitters exist in research.

tech_risk.why: Transition control at 2-5 m altitude in gusts, tipping over above ~6-7 m/s wind, and still a UAS legally.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: A follow-camera's endurance problem disappears if it never hovers to wait. With gravity paying for the glide and snow providing a free perch, hover is <10 % of airborne time.
concepts.falsification_test: Sim the transition and an upright snow landing in 0-9 m/s wind. Falsified if energy per run exceeds 0.6 Wh or more than 10 % of landings tip over.

sim_plan.what_to_model: 6-DoF tail-sitter with post-stall polar, prop wash; snow contact model

prior_art.name: Tail-sitter UAV hover research (Int J Sustainable Aviation 2023)

concepts.verdict: TOP-2. A real endurance fix for free flyers (~5x a hover-only follow drone). Biggest risk: transition control and perch stability in wind. It remains a drone for regulatory purposes.

concepts.name_en: Ram-air micro-parafoil follower (soft wing self-inflated by the skier's apparent wind)
concepts.name_zh: 冲压微型翼伞跟拍（由滑行相对风自充气）
concepts.one_liner: A 0.03 m2 soft canopy packs into 0.2 L and is inflated by the skier's own apparent wind on release, then follows by gravity with brake-line steering.
concepts.principle: Soft and packable, but a parafoil's L/D (~3) needs slopes of 19.5 deg or more, and its speed window is narrow (8-14 m/s).

architecture.carrier: ram-air canopy 0.31 m span + 110 g pod
architecture.use_flow: release from pack pocket at speed

concepts.bold_hypothesis: A soft wing is the safest gravity follower.
concepts.novelty: Guided parafoils exist for payload delivery; none for following people.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: L/D about 3 gives gravity-following on only 17 % of skiing time; the speed window is 8.2-13.8 m/s.

concepts.name_en: Aerotow camera: gravity glider on a near-zero-tension leash with a hip reel
concepts.name_zh: 滑翔拖拍：近零张力牵绳 + 髋部卷线器的重力滑翔相机
concepts.one_liner: A 125 g folding-wing glider flies 7 m behind and 3.5 m above the skier. The slope pays for the flight, and a 0.17 mm leash only adds the missing drag on flats or in headwind (median 0.01 N, p99 0.4 N). A hip reel launches the glider by sled-tow and winch, and docks it automatically into a hip quiver when the skier stops.
concepts.principle: Anything that keeps a constant height above the snow while moving with the skier must lose height at the terrain drop rate Vc*sin(theta). A glider loses height at Va/(L/D). With L/D 7-12 at 8-12 m/s, gravity alone pays for following on slopes steeper than about 5.5 deg in still air. That covers 85 % of an assumed blue/red day. Where it falls short (flats, headwind), the skier tows it like a sailplane on aerotow. The tow needs only the energy deficit, about drag minus gravity, so the line tension is the size of drag (~W/(L/D)), not of weight. A kite needs tether tension of the order of its weight or more, which in round 1 was 12-38 N. The same line does three more jobs: it caps fly-away, provides winch launch from a standstill, and pulls the glider into a funnel dock. Snow is the soft fallback surface.

architecture.carrier: 125 g foam/carbon glider, S 0.06 m2, span 0.73 m AR 9, spring-hinged wings fold aft along the fuselage (tube-launched-UAV style), split-flap airbrake, belly skid
architecture.support: aerodynamic lift; leash carries only drag deficit (p99 0.4 N)
architecture.energy: gravity (slope) + skier tow on flats; 3.7 Wh 1S cell for avionics/camera (2.9 W); 10 Wh hip cell runs the reel and tops up the glider in the quiver
architecture.sensing: UWB ranging to hip tag + GNSS + IMU; reel line length/angle encoder gives relative position directly (the leash is a position sensor)
architecture.imaging: 16 g 4K camera with gyro log (RunCam Thumb Pro class), 90 deg HFOV after EIS crop, subject-tracking reframe; no gimbal
architecture.use_flow: arm at top -> push off -> glider drops from quiver, sled-towed over snow, winch-launched at skier 4 m/s -> gravity follow -> on deceleration reel pulls it down the line into the hip funnel (wings fold) -> lift ride docked & charging

viewpoints.notes: 429 px (4K, 90 deg); lateral offset of +-3-5 m is possible for 3/4 rear views (ASSUMED, needs sim)

LDmax.ref: calc_slope_glider.py parabolic polar cd0 0.035 e 0.8 (ASSUMED at Re 65k)

jitter_bg_wind6.ref: von Karman surface-layer ASSUMED; wind 9 m/s -> 2.14

filming_per_charge.ref: 3.7 Wh, -10 C 0.75, 10 % reserve, 2.9 W; topped up from hip cell

criteria_estimate.avail: ~85-90 % (ASSUMED: launch 5 s per segment, 2 % over KE cap)
criteria_estimate.azRange: ~60-90 deg if lateral offset flown (needs sim)

footage.why: Real chase-plane view from behind and above at 7.8 m, ~430 px, decoupled from the body. Turbulence jitter is estimated at 0.7-2 deg/s. Behind-only by default.

interference.why: 425 g on the hip, no hands while skiing. Line pull is <0.6 N, below what the skier can feel.

convenience.why: Zero or one action per run; launch and dock happen while moving, standstill 0-6 s. Packs to ~2.9 L.

safety.why: KE capped at 14.9 J by a speed limit. Rider-frame strike if the rider falls is 5.5 J. A thin line behind the skier is the residual hazard, reduced by a 3 N free-running clutch.

simplicity.why: Glider autopilot, reel tension control and funnel dock. No propulsion and no hover.

originality.why: No unpowered or gravity follower and no leashed glider for a person found. The parts come from sailplane aerotow/winch, boat-towed UAV recovery and tube-launched UAVs.

tech_risk.why: The dock-on-deceleration and sled-tow launch are unproven, and the regulatory class is unclear (towed glider, kite or UAS).

concepts.bold_hypothesis: A ski slope is an unlimited, free energy source for a camera that descends with the skier. With the slope covering most of the energy, a leash that only supplies the deficit can give a towed camera body forces about 100 times lower than a kite while keeping a kite's 'can't fly away' safety.
concepts.falsification_test: Sim: 3-DoF glider + reel-controlled elastic line + calibrated skier/wind models (sim/js/concepts/common). Run 20 tracks across the slope mix, with wind -5/0/+5/gusts 9 m/s. Falsified if p95 line tension exceeds 3 N while moving, usable frames fall below 80 %, the dock succeeds in under 95 % of stops, or jitter exceeds 3 deg/s in nominal conditions. Bench (not run): pull a folded glider into the funnel at 1.5 m/s 200 times.
kill_criteria: p95 tension >3 N moving (it would become a kite)
line visible >=1 px over subject >2 % of frames
regulator classifies it as a UAS requiring VLOS by a second person (then no better than a drone legally)

concepts.name_en: Ground-effect snow skimmer (WIG follower at 0.2-0.8 m)
concepts.one_liner: Fly the glider in ground effect, low behind the skier, for a better L/D and a low cinematic angle.
concepts.principle: Ground effect only matters at h/b < 0.15. For a 0.73 m span that means 0.1 m, where moguls and skis are.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: 0.2 % L/D gain at 0.4 m, and at knee height it is a strike hazard to other skiers' legs and on moguls.

concepts.name_zh: 无动力自转向雪面跟拍舱
concepts.one_liner: A 130 g sled with a mast that slides behind the skier on gravity, braking with a drag flap.
concepts.principle: The KE cap forces 0.13-0.21 kg. At 10 m/s a mogul crest gives 5 g, so the pod goes airborne, and it sits in other skiers' paths.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: trip hazard on the piste, uncontrollable over moguls, low occluded view.

concepts.name_en: Supercapacitor sprint micro-quad recharged on the lift
concepts.name_zh: 超级电容冲刺微型机（缆车上充电）
concepts.one_liner: Lithium-free, cold-proof quad that flies 60 s highlights on a supercap topped up in 20 s.
concepts.principle: A 60 s follow needs 0.5 Wh, which at 5.4 Wh/kg is 123 g of supercap against 4 g of Li-ion.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: mass. A glider could use one (48 g), but it is not worth it over a heated Li-ion cell.

concepts.one_liner: Use solid-state ion propulsion (MIT 2018) for a silent glider-follower.
concepts.principle: Thrust 0.13 N at 5-9 N/kW needs 14-25 W against 2.5 W for a propeller, with 40 kV near people and snow and humidity.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: 6-10x the power of a propeller, and on slopes gravity needs no thrust at all.

concepts.name_en: Leapfrog lander with pole 'ring-tilt' snatch pickup
concepts.name_zh: 跃进落位 + 雪杖挑环回收
concepts.one_liner: The gravity glider runs ahead (it can fly faster than the skier's centreline), lands beside the piste 40 m ahead, raises a loop and films the skier approaching and passing. The skier hooks the loop with a pole tip at ~5 m/s, as in WWII glider snatch pickups, and the glider is relaunched from the hip.
concepts.principle: On slopes the glider has surplus energy, so it can lead instead of follow. Snow is a free tripod. Recovery uses the skier's own momentum, as in a snatch pickup.

architecture.carrier: I-01 glider + 0.5 m elastic loop mast
architecture.use_flow: lead 6.6 s -> land -> film approach -> snatch -> hip quiver

viewpoints.notes: 112 px at 30 m, 336 px at 10 m

footage.why: Classic static-camera pan shots, one per hop.

interference.why: Requires aiming the pole at speed.

convenience.why: A 20-40 % miss rate means climbing back.

originality.why: Snatch pickup by a skier is unprecedented.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: A skier can retrieve a camera on the move as reliably as hitting a slalom gate.
concepts.falsification_test: Not physically run. Sim/human-factors: falsified if pole-tip aim sigma exceeds 10 cm at 5 m/s.
kill_criteria: judged a pre-placed camera under the brief

concepts.name_en: Slope-soaring / katabatic station keeping at stops
concepts.name_zh: 坡面升力/下坡风定点盘旋
concepts.one_liner: Keep the glider aloft while the skier stands, using slope lift, the way RC slope soarers do.
concepts.principle: Needs about 1.8 m/s of upslope wind on a 20 deg slope. Over cold snow the drainage flow is usually 2-4 m/s DOWNslope, which gives sink.
concepts.verdict: KILLED as a mode the product relies on; opportunistic on windward ridges only.

concepts.one_liner: Release the glider from the chair near the top to bank 5-15 m of extra height.
concepts.principle: Gives 12 J per 10 m, which is useful, but throwing objects from a lift is illegal or against resort rules.

concepts.name_en: Shadow cam: helmet camera films the skier's own shadow
concepts.name_zh: 影子相机：头盔相机拍自己的影子
concepts.one_liner: The low winter sun projects a true third-person silhouette onto the snow; a rear/down helmet camera records it.
concepts.principle: Shadow 1.9-4.7 m long at 46 N. It is visible only with the sun behind (~1/3 of headings) and is a silhouette, not the skier.
concepts.novelty: not searched (shadow selfies are a common photo genre)
concepts.verdict: KILLED as a product (not real appearance footage); possible free bonus clip in any helmet cam.

concepts.name_en: Silicon-anode battery follow quad (cross-industry battery check)
concepts.name_zh: 硅负极电池跟拍四旋翼（跨行业电池检验）
concepts.one_liner: Apply 2025 450 Wh/kg cells (Amprius SiCore) to fix drone endurance.
concepts.principle: A 249 g quad needs about 52 W. 45 min cold needs 150 g of cells, which leaves ~100 g for everything else, and KE at 12 m/s is 17.9 J > 14.9.
concepts.verdict: KILLED: batteries do not fix the hover-power x KE corner; changing the energy source (gravity) does.
